_about: Which mapped names are peoples rather than states, for the era pages' two "Largest" lists. Read by scripts/lib/era-stats.mjs; run `npm run data:stats` after a change. Names must match the map data exactly (the build fails otherwise).

The rule: a name for a people, culture or way of life (hunter-gatherers, herders, an archaeological culture, a tribal confederation) is a people. A polity that historians treat as a state at that date stays a state, even when it carries a people's name (the Avar and Khazar khaganates, the Ostrogoth and Visigoth kingdoms of 500). A lump of several states drawn as one shape is in neither list, and so are Antarctica and a state the source draws before it existed.

An entry is a name, or { n, from?, until?, why }: it applies to eras from the year `from` and before the year `until` (BCE years negative); outside that range the name counts as a state. Anything not listed is a state.
